heading.en: What did PDRN improve more than retinol?

title.en: Crow's feet and under-eye lines fell 20–23%, against 6–7% with retinol

body.en: Each eye area was photographed in a VISIA 7, a closed booth that takes close-up pictures under the same lighting, from the same position, at every visit. Software then counted the wrinkles and measured the area they covered, at the outer corner of the eye (crow's feet) and below it.

At day 28 all four readings were 20% to 23% lower on the PDRN side, against 6% to 7% lower on the retinol side of the same faces. Crow's-feet area fell 23.0% against 6.6%, and the number of lines under the eye 23.4% against 7.0%. Each of the four gaps between the sides was significant at p < 0.001 ([Ye et al., 2026](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0350905), Figure 6B).

The gap opened early. By day 14, crow's-feet area was already 12.4% lower on the PDRN side, almost twice the 6.6% the retinol side reached by day 28 (p < 0.001 between the sides at day 14). For anyone whose first concern is the lines around the eyes, this is the trial's clearest result.

title.en: Elasticity rose 44% and firmness improved 30%, against 25% and 16% with retinol

body.en: Both were measured with a Cutometer, a small probe that draws the skin gently into its opening by suction, lets it go, and records how it moves. Elasticity (R2) is the share of the stretch the skin takes back once released: higher is more elastic. Firmness (F4) reflects how easily the skin is drawn in, and the reading falls as skin becomes firmer.

By day 28, elasticity had risen 44.0% on the PDRN side against 24.8% on the retinol side, and the firmness reading had improved 29.6% against 16.3%; both gaps were significant at p < 0.001. The PDRN side was already ahead at day 14, with elasticity up 21.3% against 14.9% (p < 0.001) and firmness improved 12.8% against 8.2% (p < 0.01) ([Ye et al., 2026](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0350905), Figure 6B).
These are the exact figures behind the authors' summary of about 1.8 times the retinol change. Retinol improved both measures as well; PDRN improved them further in the same four weeks.

title.en: The skin's deeper layer measured 11.5% thicker, against 5.5% with retinol

body.en: An Ultrascan UC22, a high-frequency ultrasound made for skin, scanned the dermis: the layer under the surface that gives skin its body. It measured how thick that layer was and how dense it looked on the scan, a percentage the instrument reads from the image.

At day 28 the layer was 11.5% thicker on the PDRN side against 5.5% with retinol, and 9.6% denser against 4.8%; both differences were significant at p < 0.001. Thickness was already ahead at day 14 (7.5% against 2.9%, p < 0.001), and so was density (4.8% against 3.0%, p < 0.05) ([Ye et al., 2026](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0350905), Figure 6B).

The authors read a four-week change like this as an early signal that is partly plumper, better-hydrated skin. Both sides of every face had the same cream base, so everyday moisturising is unlikely to explain the gap between them, and the same cream raised collagen in the team's laboratory skin samples (below).

title.en: Eye-bag volume fell 14.8%, against 10.2% with retinol

body.en: The under-eye area was mapped with an Antera 3D, a camera that builds a relief map of the skin from photographs lit from several directions. From those maps the team measured the volume of each eye bag, and the length and volume of the hollow that runs below it, the tear trough.

At day 28, eye-bag volume was 14.8% lower on the PDRN side against 10.2% with retinol (p < 0.05). The under-eye hollow improved more on the PDRN side as well: its volume fell 13.7% against 10.2%, and its length 10.4% against 6.6% (p < 0.01 for each). The hollow's volume was already ahead at day 14, at 7.4% against 5.0% (p < 0.05) ([Ye et al., 2026](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0350905), Figure 6B).
Every woman in the trial had visible eye bags when it began. Retinol eased the look of puffiness too; PDRN went further on all three under-eye measures.

heading.en: How does PDRN work on UV-damaged skin?

title.en: All nine collagens measured rose in UV-damaged skin samples

body.en: In the laboratory, the team kept pieces of full-thickness human skin alive in culture and exposed them to UVA and UVB light four times, a day apart. After each exposure they applied the same 0.1% PDRN eye cream the women used, then once a day for three more days. Comparison samples had the same light and plain culture medium. Thin slices were then stained for each protein, and the stain was measured under the microscope.

Against the untreated UV-damaged samples, every one of the nine collagens was significantly higher. The two main structural collagens, types I and III, rose 82% and 69%; the largest rises were in types VI and VII (232% and 191%), the smallest in type XV (21%). The living part of the outer layer was thicker too. These are laboratory findings in skin samples, three per group ([Ye et al., 2026](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0350905), Figure 5).

No people, no labels or branding, nothing drawn travelling into skin. Suggested file name: skingenetix-pdrn-uv-damaged-skin-samples-culture-plate.jpg.

title.en: Elastin rose 36% and fibrillin-1 115% in the same skin samples

body.en: Skin springs back because of its elastic fibres, built from elastin laid along a framework of fibrillin-1. In the same UV-damaged human skin samples, in the laboratory, the cream raised elastin by 36% and fibrillin-1 by 115% compared with the untreated samples ([Ye et al., 2026](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0350905), Figure 5).

This is the laboratory side of the elasticity result on the women's faces, where the Cutometer reading rose 44% on the PDRN side against 25% with retinol. The skin samples show which fibres changed; the faces show elasticity changing in people. Both point the same way.

No people, no labels, no diagram of fibres or of anything entering skin. Suggested file name: skingenetix-pdrn-skin-sample-stained-section-slide.jpg.

title.en: In skin cells, collagen gene activity roughly doubled, through three cell signals

body.en: In the laboratory, the team added a small amount of PDRN-850K (0.5 micrograms per millilitre) to human fibroblasts, the skin cells that make collagen, grown in dishes. After two days, the genes for collagen types I and III were about twice as active as in untreated cells (p < 0.01 and p < 0.05, three repeats).

Within six hours, three of the cells' internal signals were stronger: TGF-β, their main instruction to make collagen, about five times higher; PI3K–Akt, which helps keep them alive and productive; and autophagy, their recycling system. Blocking any one of the three cancelled the rise in the collagen genes. In plain terms, in the laboratory PDRN worked through the cells' own collagen-making controls ([Ye et al., 2026](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0350905), Figure 1).
